title: Protected Bike Lane Networks — Core Overview (Edition 1)
description: Protected bike lanes use curbs, planters, or parked cars to separate cyclists from motor traffic, sharply increasing ridership. Networks matter more than isolated lanes, since connected grids let people ride door to door. This overview edition presents Protected Bike Lane Networks as a core mobility concept for contemporary cities.

real_examples.fact: Copenhagen's continuous protected network makes cycling a dominant commute mode.

spec.source_note: Core facts verified from public sources.
